partner_context.their_ambition: Yango is the Dubai-headquartered global ride-tech platform operating across the Middle East, Africa, the Caspian and South Asia. Critically — and this is the lead frame for every conversation — this is the **Dubai-HQ'd Yango**, headquartered and operationally based in the UAE, with its growth centred on the GCC, Africa and emerging coastal markets. That footprint maps almost perfectly onto the world's most underbuilt waterfronts: lagoon megacities, Gulf jetty networks, Red Sea resorts and Caspian bays where the road is congested and the water is empty.

hero.title: Yango × Navier — the water tier for the Dubai-HQ'd global ride platform
hero.subtitle: From Dubai's jetties to the West African lagoons and the Caspian shore — a foiling water tier in the Yango app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Yango-branded electric-foiling water-mobility tier across Yango's strongest coastal markets — anchored in its home UAE, spanning the West African lagoon cities (Abidjan, Dakar), the GCC (Qatar), Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, the Caspian shore, and Latin America's Caribbean and Pacific coasts (Cartagena, Lima) — booked in the same Yango app, on the same wallet, as the car.

why_now: Yango is scaling aggressively beyond ride-hailing into a multimodal super-app, exactly as Navier's N30 Pioneer II becomes commercially available. Yango's geography is uniquely water-shaped: Dubai (its HQ) has the densest luxury-jetty network on earth; Abidjan and Dakar are lagoon-and-island cities choked by bridges; and the Red Sea, the Caspian and Latin America's coasts are building marine-first tourism. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the dense short-water corridors across all of them, with Quanta-LR staged honestly for the longer regional legs.

network_thesis.headline: One app. Every waterway. From the Gulf to West Africa, the Caspian and Latin America.
network_thesis.body: Yango already moves millions of riders across the Gulf, Africa, the Caucasus and Latin America — and in almost every one of those cities the demand doesn't stop at the shoreline. The busiest trips — airport-to-marina, island hops, cross-bay commutes, resort transfers — are exactly where the road runs out and a boat is the fastest way across. Navier gives Yango one uniform, electric-hydrofoil fleet that riders book the same way they book a car: one tap, same app, same experience whether they're in Dubai, Dakar, Baku or Cartagena. Start with the UAE flagship, add coastlines one at a time, or commit to the whole network.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each market below is a complete phased proposal — the waterways where a fast, quiet boat changes the journey most. The UAE is the home-market flagship; the Gulf, Egypt, West Africa, the Caspian and Latin America follow one coastline at a time.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Yango operates across the Gulf, Africa, the Caucasus and Latin America. These sub-proposals are the coastlines where foiling water routes matter most — the UAE and Qatar jetties, the Nile and Alexandria, the West African lagoons of Abidjan and Dakar, the Caspian at Baku and Aktau, the Maghreb marina coast, and the Caribbean and Pacific shores of Colombia and Peru.

multimodal_fit: Same Yango app, same wallet, same account: a Yango car to the jetty, a foiling hop across the bay or lagoon, a Yango ride on arrival. In Yango's home UAE and across its African strongholds, the multimodal water leg is frequently the fastest part of the journey — and it never leaves the Yango ecosystem.
differentiation: Against Yango's incumbent competitors, a foiling water tier is a category nobody else offers — a defensible, premium, all-electric mode on exactly the congested-bridge and slow-ferry corridors where Yango's markets hurt most. Against the diesel ferries and water taxis it replaces: faster, quiet, low-wake, zero-local-emission and on-demand. Against road: a direct line that skips the gridlock.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Prove (UAE home-market flagship + first African lagoon)
phases.narrative: Launch the dense intra-Dubai jetty network in Yango's home market on Pioneer II, alongside a first proven African lagoon anchor (Abidjan). Prove economics where willingness-to-pay is highest and demand is densest.
phases.rationale: Anchor on the home-market flagship and a proven lagoon-commute base before spreading; highest-density, lowest-friction water.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Scale (Africa + GCC + Egypt + Latin America, N30 + N35)
phases.narrative: Replicate the proven playbook across the West African lagoon and coastal cities (Abidjan, Dakar, Maputo), the GCC (Doha Bay), Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, and Latin America's Caribbean and Pacific coasts (Cartagena, Lima) — adding the N35 Shuttle on the densest corridors to roughly double throughput per hull.
phases.rationale: Spoke-by-spoke rollout across Yango's strongest markets once the flagship proves the model; N35 lifts peak-corridor economics.

phases.label: Phase 3 — Mature & extend (Quanta-LR regional reach + Caspian + in-app default)
phases.narrative: Open the Quanta-LR regional and trans-water legs (Dubai–Abu Dhabi already in Pioneer range, and the Caspian crossings staged honestly), reach the Caspian market (Aktau), and mature into induced demand and the full in-app standard-operator role across the network.
phases.rationale: Honest long-range staging plus Navier becoming the standard operator and earning ride revenue once the dense network is proven; held/sovereign markets (Israel) remain data-only until coordination clears.

the_ask: Co-launch a Yango-branded foiling water tier — anchor in Yango's home UAE with a 3-boat Pioneer II flagship across Dubai's jetties, prove a first African lagoon market in parallel, then roll out spoke-by-spoke across Africa, the GCC, Egypt, the Caspian and Latin America on the shared corridor network.
close: Yango's Dubai-HQ'd, Africa-and-GCC-heavy footprint is the best-shaped ride-platform geography in the world for water mobility: its busiest markets are lagoon cities, Gulf jetty networks and congested waterfront metros where a foiling tier is both a category nobody else has and the fastest leg of the journey. The home market proves it; the network scales it.
end_state: A Yango water tier spanning its home UAE flagship, the West African lagoon cities, the GCC, Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, the Caspian, and Latin America's Caribbean and Pacific coasts — one shared corridor network, rendered as Yango's branded view, booked in the Yango app.

Senegal is a flagship of Yango's African growth story, and the water links that matter most — Dakar to Gorée, to Ngor, to Hann Bay — are today run on ageing public chaloupes and informal pirogues on fixed timetables.

revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $241M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

revenue_potential.cite_rule: Cite MID. 'High' stacks every optimistic assumption — ceiling, not headline.

rungs.label: SOM floor (published) — sourced corridors today
rungs.basis: sourced flagship corridors · 11% capture · today's demand

rungs.label: SOM full network (~11% capture, today, +greenfield)
rungs.basis: whole mapped network · 11% capture · today's demand (no growth assumed)

rungs.label: SAM matured network — induced demand at scale
rungs.basis: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market · leading-operator 25% capture, network-wide

rungs.label: Marine mobility TAM — total addressable water-transfer spend
rungs.basis: SAM divided by leading-operator capture — the full inducible water-transfer wallet at network maturity

rungs.label: Journey GMV — food, stays, and experiences (~3× TAM)
rungs.basis: add food, stays, and experiences to every crossing in the induced market

rungs.label: Partner platform revenue on Navier
rungs.basis: platform commission on journey GMV routed through the Navier network (subset of full Journey GMV)

ceiling_sibling.label: Platform revenue ceiling — 18% × full Journey GMV
ceiling_sibling.derivation: journey_gmv.mid × 0.18 (full GMV ceiling, not Navier-corridor subset)
ceiling_sibling._doc: Sibling reference. Do NOT promote to a 7th ladder rung. Platform_rev rung remains the Navier-subset Interpretation-A value.

phase_economics.headline: Revenue potential by phase — conservative floor first, ecosystem prize last.
phase_economics.conversion_note: Fleet & CO2 scale from the grounded unit: 86 boats = $26M transport rev = 8,194 t CO2/yr (~$302K rev/boat).

vessel_sizing.headline: Right vessel for every leg — corridor range picks the hull.

classes.role: Capillary corridors ≤ 70nm. The workhorse of Prove + Scale.
Doubles throughput per hull on dense corridors; roughly halves payback. Scale-phase workhorse.
Regional legs 75–150nm beyond Pioneer range. Held out of near-term numbers.

vessel_sizing.range_gate_note: ≤ 70nm → Pioneer II (now). 75–150nm → Quanta-LR (roadmap). Long legs never faked on a 70nm boat.

ladder_transitions.headline: Same 10% capture, expanded to the full mapped network
ladder_transitions.basis: Width-only step. Capture rate held at 10%; corridor set expands from sourced flagships to the full mapped network.

ladder_transitions.headline: Network matures: faster, more comfortable boats grow the market + leading-operator capture
ladder_transitions.basis: Two-lever step. (1) Faster, more comfortable boats grow the cross-water market (induced demand). (2) Leading-operator capture lifts share from 10% floor to 25% mature, network-wide.

ladder_transitions.headline: Lens shift: Navier captured share → total inducible marine-transfer wallet
ladder_transitions.basis: Unit change. Divide SAM (the captured share) by leading-operator capture rate to recover the full inducible water-transfer market — the marine-mobility TAM.

ladder_transitions.headline: Marine transfer → total journey wallet (food, stays, experiences, in-app ads)
ladder_transitions.basis: Journey-wallet step. Each $1 of marine-transfer spend unlocks ~$3 of broader journey GMV across merchants the partner monetizes.

ladder_transitions.headline: Yango platform take on Navier-carried journeys
ladder_transitions.basis: Platform-take step. Platform commission applied to the journey GMV routed through the Navier network (Navier-captured subset, not the full induced market).
ladder_transitions._lb_ref: LB-113: partner_platform_rev_on_navier = on-Navier subset, distinct from deck's '18% × full Journey GMV' narrative ceiling
